docs.title: Common Knowledge Scout Documentation
docs.text:
Common Knowledge Scout turns the files in your own storage — audio, video, PDFs, images and web pages — into structured Markdown, and makes the result available as a gallery, a website and a chat that answers with sources.

For an overview of what the application does, see the README on GitHub.

docs.title: MongoDB Vector Search (architecture)
docs.text: Status: active Last verified: 2026-01-06

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This document describes the data model and index shape for MongoDB Atlas Vector Search in this repo. Operational “what to debug” notes live in docs/analysis/ingestion.md.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• Vector collection: MongoDB collection vectors__${libraryId} (one per library)
  • Vector search index: Atlas search index vector_search_idx
  • meta: metadata-only document (no embedding)
  • chunk: text chunk + embedding
  • chapterSummary: chapter summary + embedding

This project uses MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for semantic search and RAG. Embeddings and metadata live in MongoDB. No separate vector database is required.

docs.title: Cluster-Anforderung (wichtig)
docs.text:
• Atlas Search / Vector Search läuft nur auf MongoDB Atlas (nicht auf Self-Hosted-MongoDB).
  • Auf M0 (Free)- und Flex-Clustern sind createSearchIndexes und listSearchIndexes nicht unterstützt (laut Unsupported Commands, z. B. getSearchIndexes).
  • Für Vector Search wird ein kostenpflichtiger Cluster (M2 oder höher) benötigt. Auf M0 erscheinen in Compass unter „Search Indexes“ keine Indizes, und die Anwendung meldet „Index nicht gefunden“ trotz Klick auf „Index anlegen“.

docs.title: Collection layout
docs.text:
• One collection per library: vectors__${libraryId}
  • Multiple document kinds live in the same collection (distinguished by kind)
  • meta: full metadata (no embedding)
  • chunk: text chunk + embedding
  • chapterSummary: chapter summary + embedding

docs.title: Why we keep meta without embeddings
docs.text:
• The gallery and facet aggregation need full metadata.
  • Storing meta without embeddings saves space and keeps writes cheaper.

docs.title: Vector search index
docs.text:
• Index name: vector_search_idx
  • Created lazily (first access) via Mongo admin commands

Example (simplified): 

{
  "name": "vector_search_idx",
  "definition": {
    "mappings": {
      "dynamic": true,
      "fields": {
        "embedding": {
          "type": "knnVector",
          "dimensions": 1024,
          "similarity": "cosine"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Token indexes for filtering (important)
docs.text:
Atlas Vector Search requires fields used in $vectorSearch.filter to be indexed in a compatible way. In practice, this means:

  • fields filtered via $in must be indexed as token (not plain string)
  • this includes arrays (e.g. authors, tags) and also “single string facets” if the code always uses $in

If you see errors like:

Path 'authors' needs to be indexed as token

the fix is to ensure the search index mapping contains token entries for those fields.

docs.title: Recommended mapping additions (example)
docs.text:
{
  "mappings": {
    "dynamic": true,
    "fields": {
      "embedding": { "type": "knnVector", "dimensions": 1024, "similarity": "cosine" },
      "kind": { "type": "token" },
      "libraryId": { "type": "token" },
      "user": { "type": "token" },
      "fileId": { "type": "token" },
      "authors": { "type": "token" },
      "speakers": { "type": "token" },
      "tags": { "type": "token" },
      "topics": { "type": "token" }
    }
  }
}

Notes: - The exact list depends on which facet fields you use in filters. - When in doubt: index every filterable facet as token to avoid runtime failures.

docs.title: Query patterns
docs.text:
Vector search query (simplified): 

const pipeline = [
  {
    $vectorSearch: {
      index: 'vector_search_idx',
      path: 'embedding',
      queryVector,
      numCandidates: Math.max(topK * 10, 100),
      limit: topK,
      filter: {
        kind: { $in: ['chunk', 'chapterSummary'] },
        libraryId: { $eq: libraryId },
        user: { $eq: userEmail },
      }
    }
  },
  { $project: { _id: 1, score: { $meta: 'vectorSearchScore' } } }
]

Direct Mongo query (no vector search), e.g. for neighbor chunks: 

const chunks = await collection.find({
  kind: 'chunk',
  libraryId,
  user: userEmail,
  fileId: { $in: fileIds },
}).sort({ fileId: 1, chunkIndex: 1 }).toArray()

docs.title: Facet duplication
docs.text: Facet fields are copied into chunk and chapterSummary documents so filtering can happen directly inside $vectorSearch.

docs.title: PDF Transformation Phases
docs.text: Status: active Last verified: 2026-01-06

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This document describes the current PDF processing pipeline (Extract → Template → Ingestion) and how it maps to the external-jobs runtime. It also documents the artifact contracts (Shadow‑Twin) that downstream UI and ingestion rely on.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• Transcript: extracted Markdown without frontmatter (Phase 1 output)
  • Transformation: template-based Markdown with frontmatter/metadata (Phase 2 output)
  • Ingestion: RAG upsert into MongoDB Atlas Vector Search (Phase 3)
  • Shadow‑Twin: derived artifacts stored next to the source file (often in a dot-folder)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PDF transformation consists of three sequential phases that convert a PDF file into a searchable, structured document ready for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation). Each phase builds upon the previous one, creating intermediate artifacts that can be reused or skipped based on policies.

In the current implementation (IST), these three phases are not executed via three separate HTTP endpoints, but through a combination of:

  • Worker: src/lib/external-jobs-worker.ts – polls jobs and calls the start route
  • Start route: src/app/api/external/jobs/[jobId]/start/route.ts – initializes the job and starts Phase 1 (Extract) or an ingest-only path
  • Secretary Service (external) – performs PDF/OCR/template transformation and sends webhooks back
  • Callback route: src/app/api/external/jobs/[jobId]/route.ts – processes webhooks and orchestrates Phase 1–3 (Extract, Template, Ingestion)

docs.title: Runtime Orchestration (high level)
docs.text:
Worker (jobs queue)
  ↓ POST /api/external/jobs/{jobId}/start
Start route
  - loads PDF from storage
  - decides Extract/Template/Ingest-only via gates + policies
  - calls Secretary Service (PDF/OCR)
  ↓ Webhook: POST /api/external/jobs/{jobId}
Secretary Service (external)
  - extracts text/images
  - sends extracted_text, pages_archive_url, mistral_ocr_raw_url, ...
  ↓
Callback route
  - processes extract result (Phase 1)
  - runs or skips template phase (Phase 2)
  - runs or skips ingestion (Phase 3)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Extract text and images from PDF files using OCR or native text extraction.

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. PDF Processing:
  2. PDF file is sent to Secretary Service
  3. Text extraction via native PDF parsing or OCR (Mistral OCR)

  4. Image extraction (if enabled)

  5. Image Processing:

  6. Mistral OCR images: Extracted via mistral_ocr_images_url (ZIP archive) - separate from mistral_ocr_raw
  7. PDF page images: Extracted as ZIP archive (pages_archive_url or pages_archive_data)
  8. Images saved to Shadow-Twin directory (if present)

  9. Note: Asynchronous webhook sends mistral_ocr_raw_url and mistral_ocr_raw_metadata only. Full mistral_ocr_raw data must be downloaded via GET /api/pdf/jobs/{job_id}/mistral-ocr-raw

  10. Markdown Creation:

  11. Extracted text saved as Markdown without frontmatter
  12. File name (v2): {baseName}.{language}.md (transcript, language suffix)

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• PDF file (document.pdf)
  • Extraction method (native or mistral_ocr)
  • Target language (for OCR)
  • Image extraction flags (includeOcrImages, includePageImages)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Transcript File: document.de.md (Markdown without frontmatter; language suffix)
  • Images: Saved to .document.pdf/ directory (if images extracted)
  • Shadow-Twin Directory: Created automatically if images are present

docs.title: Code References (IST)
docs.text:
• Worker & routes
  • src/lib/external-jobs-worker.ts: Background worker that polls jobs from the queue and triggers the start route (POST /api/external/jobs/[jobId]/start)
  • src/app/api/external/jobs/[jobId]/start/route.ts: Start route; loads the PDF from storage, sets watchdog/steps, calls Secretary Service (standard or Mistral OCR endpoint) and can run an ingest-only flow
  • src/app/api/external/jobs/[jobId]/route.ts: Callback route; processes webhooks from Secretary Service (including extracted_text, pages_archive_url, mistral_ocr_raw_url) and decides whether to run Extract-only, Extract+Template+Ingest or a skip path
  • Extract-Phase (Core-Module)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/extract-only.ts: Extract-only processing logic (Transcript speichern, Bilder verarbeiten, Job abschließen)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/images.ts: Image extraction and processing (pages-Archive, images-Archive, Mistral OCR)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/storage.ts: Markdown storage in the shadow twin or parent folder
  • src/lib/processing/gates.ts (gateExtractPdf): Gate that checks whether a shadow twin (transcript or transformed) already exists and allows Extract to be skipped
  • src/lib/transform/image-extraction-service.ts: Image extraction service (deeper image-processing pipeline)

docs.title: Execution in Code (IST)
docs.text:
• Start route
  • Loads the PDF from storage via getServerProvider.
  • Runs preprocessing and initializes steps (extract_pdf, transform_template, ingest_rag).
  • Calls gateExtractPdf and phase policies to decide:
    • whether Extract should actually be sent to Secretary Service (runExtract),
    • whether only Template/Ingestion should run,
    • whether an ingest-only path without a new Secretary call is possible.

  • When runExtract is true, sends an HTTP request to Secretary Service (/api/pdf/process or /api/pdf/process-mistral-ocr) with callback_url = /api/external/jobs/{jobId}.

  • Callback route

  • Receives webhooks with extracted_text and image archives.
  • Marks extract_pdf as completed as soon as a stable OCR result is available.
  • If template and ingest phases are explicitly disabled, calls runExtractOnly, stores the transcript without frontmatter and optionally processes images.
  • In all other cases it only ensures that Phase 1 is completed and passes the results to the template/ingestion logic.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Add structured metadata (frontmatter) to the extracted text, enabling structured queries and RAG integration.

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. Template Processing:
  2. Transcript Markdown (document.md) is sent to Secretary Service template transformer
  3. LLM analyzes content and extracts structured metadata
  4. Frontmatter is generated with chapters, topics etc.

  5. The total page count (pages) is not computed by the template but always reconstructed from the --- Seite N --- markers in the Markdown body.

  6. Markdown Creation:

  7. Transcript content + frontmatter = transformed Markdown
  8. File name: {originalName}.{language}.md (with language suffix - transformed)

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• Transcript Markdown (document.md)
  • Template content (structured schema)
  • Target language

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Transformed File: document.de.md (Markdown with frontmatter)
  • Metadata: Structured data in YAML frontmatter

docs.title: Code References (IST)
docs.text:
• Routes & orchestration
  • src/app/api/external/jobs/[jobId]/route.ts: Central callback route that, after receiving extract results, decides whether the template phase runs or is skipped and then saves the transformed Markdown.
  • Template phase (core modules)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/phase-template.ts: Consolidated template phase (decision logic, repair cases, saving transformed Markdown)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/template-run.ts: Template transformation execution (calls the Secretary template transformer and parses the response)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/chapters.ts: Chapter detection and merge based on text
  • src/lib/external-jobs/template-files.ts: Template-Auswahl für External Jobs (MongoDB Source of Truth), serialisiert Secretary-kompatibel (ohne creation)
  • src/lib/templates/template-service-mongodb.ts: MongoDB Template-Service inkl. Serialisierung zu Template-Markdown (Frontmatter + Body + systemprompt)
  • Hinweis (Legacy): src/lib/templates/template-service.ts lädt Templates aus dem Library-Storage /templates Ordner und wird primär für Import/Migration genutzt.
  • src/lib/processing/gates.ts (gateTransformTemplate): Gate checking (e.g. skip if chapter metadata already exists)
  • src/lib/external-jobs/storage.ts: Saves transformed Markdown ({originalName}.{language}.md)

docs.title: Execution in Code (IST)
docs.text:
• Callback route
  • Runs a preprocess span (if not already present) to detect existing frontmatter and its quality.
  • Reads policies and phase flags via readPhasesAndPolicies and job.parameters.phases.
  • Determines from the callback body whether chapter metadata (chapters) is already present.
  • Calls the consolidated template phase (runTemplatePhase in phase-template.ts), which:
    • combines policies (metadata: force/skip/auto/ignore),
    • gates (gateTransformTemplate), and
    • the repair needs of an existing shadow twin.
  • Template transformation is only executed if no chapter metadata (chapters) exists yet. If only pages are missing, they are reconstructed from the --- Seite N --- markers in the body.
  • When template processing is executed:
    • it selects a template from MongoDB (TemplateDocument) and serialisiert es als Secretary-kompatibles Template-Markdown (ohne creation),
    • calls the Secretary template endpoint and adds chapter information,
    • strips old frontmatter and stores the new Markdown with frontmatter via saveMarkdown as {originalName}.{language}.md,
    • and reliably marks the transform_template step as completed or failed.
  • When the template phase is skipped (chapters already exist), only missing pages are reconstructed and the existing frontmatter is used directly as the basis for ingestion.

docs.title: Skip Conditions
docs.text:
• Chapter metadata (chapters) already exists (frontmatter is complete with respect to chapters).
  • Template phase disabled via policy.
  • Previous job already completed the template phase.

If only the page count (pages) is missing, the template phase is skipped and pages is silently reconstructed from the --- Seite N --- markers in the body.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Ingest transformed Markdown into MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for RAG queries.

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. Markdown Processing:
  2. Transformed Markdown (document.de.md) is parsed
  3. Images are processed and uploaded to Azure Storage (Slides, Cover, Markdown images)

  4. Final Markdown (with Azure image URLs) is stored in MongoDB

  5. Vector Storage:

  6. Complete document is sent to Secretary Service RAG API (/api/rag/embed-text)
  7. Secretary Service performs Markdown-aware chunking and embedding generation
  8. Chunks with embeddings are received and stored in MongoDB Vector Search Collection
  9. Meta-documents (without embeddings) are stored alongside chunks for gallery display

  10. Facet metadata is duplicated into chunks for direct filtering during vector search

  11. MongoDB Storage:

  12. All data stored in MongoDB: Meta-documents, chunks, and chapter summaries in same collection
  13. Collection structure: vectors__${libraryId} per library
  14. Document metadata stored as kind: 'meta' documents (no embeddings)

  15. Chapter summaries stored as kind: 'chapterSummary' documents (with embeddings)

  16. Image Upload (Shadow-Twin → Azure Storage):

  17. All image handling in Phase 3 is based on the Shadow-Twin directory and is centralized in the ingestion service.
  18. Session-mode documents (events with slides):
    • docMetaJson.slides[].image_url is interpreted as a reference into the Shadow-Twin.
    • Each slide image is resolved via findShadowTwinImage, uploaded to Azure Storage under the scoped path …/{libraryId}/sessions/{fileId}/{hash}.{ext} and de-duplicated by hash.
    • The resulting Azure URLs replace the original slides[].image_url values and are used directly by the frontend (EventSlides).
  19. Book-mode documents (no slides):
    • A cover image is detected in the Shadow-Twin directory (preview_001.jpg), uploaded to Azure under …/{libraryId}/books/{fileId}/{hash}.{ext} and stored as docMetaJson.coverImageUrl; this field is also available as a facet and is used by the gallery and book-detail views.
    • Inline images in the Markdown body (Markdown ![](), HTML <img> and Obsidian <img-x.ext> syntax) are resolved against the Shadow-Twin, uploaded to Azure under the books scope and all references in the Markdown are rewritten to use the Azure URLs.
  20. Frontend components (gallery cards, document detail, markdown viewer) use only these Azure URLs; direct access to Shadow-Twin image files from the browser is no longer required.

docs.title: Execution in Code (IST)
docs.text:
• Start route (ingest-only path)

  • If policies/gates decide that Extract/Template are not needed but ingestion should run:

    • it searches for the already transformed Markdown in the shadow twin (directory first, then file),
    • loads the Markdown text and parses frontmatter via parseSecretaryMarkdownStrict,
    • calls runIngestion directly and completes the job after successful ingestion.

  • Callback route (regular path)

  • Uses gateIngestRag and optionally ingestionCheck to determine whether vectors for this document already exist in the MongoDB Vector Search collection.
  • Reads ingestion policies (ingestPolicy: 'do' | 'force' | 'skip' plus legacy flags from job.parameters).
  • Determines useIngestion and marks ingest_rag as skipped if appropriate (including reason).
  • When ingestion runs:
    • determines fileId and fileName of the document to ingest,
    • loads Markdown for ingestion (directly from the current callback context or via storage fallback),
    • calls runIngestion, which:
    • calls IngestionService.upsertMarkdown(...),
    • stores chunks in Pinecone, and
    • writes metadata (including chapter summaries) to MongoDB,
    • updates the ingestion status in the job (setIngestion) and sets the ingest_rag step to completed.
  • Finally calls setJobCompleted, updates the shadow-twin state to processingStatus: 'ready' and sends a final job_update event with refreshFolderIds.

docs.title: Skip Conditions
docs.text:
• Document already ingested (check via ingestionCheck)
  • Ingestion phase disabled via policy

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
Phases can be controlled via policies:

interface PhasePolicies {
  extract: 'force' | 'skip' | 'auto' | 'ignore';
  metadata: 'force' | 'skip' | 'auto' | 'ignore';
  ingest: 'force' | 'skip' | 'auto' | 'ignore';
}
  • force: Always execute phase (even if artifacts exist)
  • skip: Skip phase (even if artifacts don't exist)
  • auto: Execute if needed (check gates)
  • ignore: Phase disabled

docs.title: Gates
docs.text:
Gates check if phases should be skipped:

  • gateExtractPdf(): Checks for existing Shadow-Twin files
  • gateTransformTemplate(): Checks for existing frontmatter
  • gateIngestRag(): Checks for existing ingestion

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text:
PDF File
  ↓
[Gate: Extract] → Skip if Shadow-Twin exists
  ↓
Phase 1: Extract → document.md + images
  ↓
[Gate: Template] → Skip if frontmatter exists
  ↓
Phase 2: Template → document.de.md
  ↓
[Gate: Ingestion] → Skip if already ingested
  ↓
Phase 3: Ingestion → Vector storage + MongoDB
  ↓
Complete

docs.title: v2-only artifact naming (Shadow‑Twin)
docs.text: In the current runtime, file naming is deterministic and shared across all media types. Do not rely on legacy “originalName.md” heuristics.

docs.title: Transcript artifact (Phase 1)
docs.text:
• Format: {baseName}.{language}.md
  • Example: document.de.md
  • Content: extracted Markdown (typically without frontmatter)

docs.title: Transformation artifact (Phase 2)
docs.text:
• Format: {baseName}.{templateName}.{language}.md
  • Example: document.pdfanalyse.de.md
  • Content: Markdown with frontmatter/metadata

docs.title: Location
docs.text: Artifacts can live either: 1) inside a dot-folder .{originalName}/ (recommended when multiple assets exist), or 2) as siblings next to the PDF (common when only Markdown exists).

docs.title: Update semantics
docs.text: Re-running the same phase updates (overwrites) the canonical artifact instead of creating duplicates.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Phase failures: Logged in job document, job status set to failed
  • Partial completion: Intermediate artifacts preserved
  • Retry: Failed phases can be retried independently
  • Skip on error: Subsequent phases can still execute if previous phase failed (depending on policy)

docs.title: Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Parallel processing: Images processed in parallel with text extraction
  • Caching: Secretary Service caches OCR results
  • Batch processing: Multiple PDFs processed in parallel
  • Incremental updates: Only changed phases re-executed

docs.title: Shadow‑Twin (architecture)
docs.text:
Status: active Last verified: 2026-01-06

User-facing overview: docs/guides/shadow-twin.md

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This document describes the intended storage model and contracts for Shadow‑Twin artifacts in the current system. It is intentionally focused on naming, layout, and resolver/writer contracts (not UI details).

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
• Source file: the original file (PDF/audio/video/image/…).
  • Shadow‑Twin: derived artifacts (Markdown + assets) stored next to the source.
  • Transcript: extracted text as Markdown (typically without frontmatter).
  • Transformation: template-based Markdown with frontmatter/metadata.
  • Dot-folder: hidden folder .{originalName} grouping multiple related artifacts.

docs.title: Concept
docs.text:
A Shadow‑Twin is the text/metadata representation of an original file (PDF, audio, video, image, …). It may include: - Markdown artifacts (transcript + transformation) - Images/assets (e.g. extracted from PDFs)

Shadow‑Twins exist to enable: - searchability - structured metadata - reliable downstream ingestion / RAG

docs.title: User story mapping (how this feels in the UI)
docs.text:
Even for expert users, the mental model is usually intent-driven, not file-driven. We therefore describe the pipeline as a 3‑step story:

  1. Text erzeugen (media-dependent)
  2. PDF/Image: OCR/Extract → transcript artifact
  3. Audio/Video: Transkription → transcript artifact
  4. Transformieren (journalistic moment)
  5. LLM/template converts raw text into structured, meaningful content → transformation artifact
  6. Veröffentlichen
  7. ingestion into the Library/RAG index → Mongo Vector Search (meta + chunks)

Storage-wise these steps map deterministically to Shadow‑Twin artifacts: - Step 1 → Transcript {base}.{lang}.md - Step 2 → Transformation {base}.{template}.{lang}.md - Step 3 → Ingestion records keyed by the source fileId (index/chunks)

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text: Shadow‑Twins have a single canonical write layout and one legacy read fallback.

docs.title: 1) Dot‑folder (canonical)
docs.text:
Hidden folder (starts with .), containing all related files:

.document.pdf/
├── document.de.md                 (Transcript)
├── document.<template>.de.md      (Transformation)
├── page-001.png                   (Extracted images)
└── ...

Folder naming: .{originalName} (e.g. .document.pdf/) Length limit: 255 characters (truncated if necessary).

docs.title: 2) Siblings (legacy read fallback only)
docs.text:
Files stored next to the original (legacy). The system may still resolve these for backwards compatibility, but new writes should not create siblings. A future repair/migration run is expected to move siblings into the dot-folder and remove them.

document.pdf
document.de.md                 (Transcript)
document.<template>.de.md      (Transformation)

docs.title: Transcript artifact
docs.text:
• Format: {baseName}.{language}.md
  • Example: document.de.md
  • Created: after Extract/Transcribe
  • Content: extracted markdown (typically without frontmatter)

docs.title: Transformation artifact
docs.text:
• Format: {baseName}.{templateName}.{language}.md
  • Example: document.pdfanalyse.de.md
  • Created: after Template transformation
  • Content: markdown with frontmatter/metadata

docs.title: Dot‑folder
docs.text:
• Format: .{originalName}
  • Example: .document.pdf/

docs.title: Resolution model (how the UI finds the “right” artifact)
docs.text:
For library browsing (e.g. file-list.tsx) the UI does not implement filename heuristics. Instead:

  1. UI calls POST /api/library/[libraryId]/artifacts/batch-resolve (in batches of ≤100).
  2. Server resolves each source via resolveArtifact():
  3. checks the dot‑folder first (if present)
  4. falls back to siblings
  5. if preferredKind === 'transformation' and no templateName is provided, the resolver selects the best matching transformation for the language (currently: newest by modifiedAt)
  6. Server returns ResolvedArtifactWithItem so the UI does not need additional per-item fetches.

Entry points: - src/app/api/library/[libraryId]/artifacts/batch-resolve/route.ts - src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-resolver.ts - src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-client.ts - src/hooks/use-shadow-twin-analysis.ts

docs.title: Writing model (how artifacts are stored)
docs.text:
Writing is centralized to avoid duplicates and to enforce deterministic updates: - writeArtifact() uses a canonical filename derived from the artifact key - if the target file already exists → it is overwritten (update, not duplicate) - optionally writes into a dot‑folder (when needed for related assets)

Entry point: - src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-writer.ts

docs.title: Code references (current)
docs.text:
• Naming & parsing: src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-naming.ts
  • Resolver: src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-resolver.ts
  • Writer: src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-writer.ts
  • Bulk API: src/app/api/library/[libraryId]/artifacts/batch-resolve/route.ts
  • Client wrapper: src/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-client.ts

docs.title: Resolve an artifact (server-side)
docs.text:
import { resolveArtifact } from '@/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-resolver';

const resolved = await resolveArtifact(provider, {
  sourceItemId,
  sourceName: 'document.pdf',
  parentId,
  targetLanguage: 'de',
  preferredKind: 'transformation',
  templateName: 'pdfanalyse',
});

docs.title: Write an artifact (server-side)
docs.text:
import { writeArtifact } from '@/lib/shadow-twin/artifact-writer';

await writeArtifact(provider, {
  key: {
    sourceId: sourceItemId,
    kind: 'transformation',
    targetLanguage: 'de',
    templateName: 'pdfanalyse',
  },
  sourceName: 'document.pdf',
  parentId,
  content: markdownWithFrontmatter,
  createFolder: true,
});

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
1. UI must not implement filename heuristics: use the bulk resolver API.
  2. Use centralized naming: buildArtifactName() for canonical filenames.
  3. Use centralized writing: writeArtifact() to enforce update semantics.
  4. Dot‑folder naming must respect the 255 char limit: rely on generateShadowTwinFolderName().

docs.title: State Architecture
docs.text:
The Library module uses a centralized state management approach with Jotai atoms:

  • Global State: Libraries list, active library
  • Navigation State: Current folder, path
  • UI State: Loading states, selected files
  • Cache: Folder items cache for performance

docs.title: 1. Folder Items Cache (folderItemsAtom)
docs.text:
The folderItemsAtom is an atom family that caches folder contents by folder ID:

// Atom family for folder-specific caching
export const folderItemsAtom = atomFamily((folderId: string) => 
  atom<StorageItem[] | null>(null)
);

How it works: - Each folder has its own cached state - When currentFolderId === 'root', root items are cached - Components can access cached items synchronously without API calls - Cache is updated when folders are loaded via StorageContext

Benefits: - Eliminates duplicate API calls for the same folder - Provides instant access to already-loaded data - Reduces server load and improves performance

docs.title: 2. Root Items Central Management (useRootItems)
docs.text:
The useRootItems hook provides centralized access to root items:

// Hook automatically uses cache if available
const getRootItems = useRootItems();

// Synchronous access if root items are already cached
const rootItems = useRootItemsSync();

How it works: - Checks folderItemsAtom if currentFolderId === 'root' - Falls back to API call via StorageContext.listItems('root') - Uses request deduplication from StorageContext - All components share the same cached root items

Integration with StorageContext: - StorageContext loads root items once when library is initialized - Updates folderItemsAtom when root items are loaded - useRootItems reads from cache, avoiding duplicate requests

docs.title: 3. Request Deduplication
docs.text:
The StorageContext implements request deduplication:

  • Multiple simultaneous requests for the same folder are merged
  • Only one API call is made, all callers receive the same promise
  • Prevents duplicate network requests during rapid navigation

docs.title: 4. State Flow
docs.text:
1. User navigates to folder
   ↓
2. StorageContext.listItems(folderId)
   ↓
3. Request deduplication checks for pending requests
   ↓
4. API call (if not cached/deduplicated)
   ↓
5. folderItemsAtom updated with results
   ↓
6. All components using folderItemsAtom receive updates

docs.title: State Atoms Reference
docs.text: Atom Type Purpose libraryAtom LibraryState Main library state container activeLibraryIdAtom string Currently active library ID librariesAtom ClientLibrary[] List of all user libraries activeLibraryAtom ClientLibrary \| undefined Active library object (derived) currentFolderIdAtom string Current folder ID (default: 'root') folderItemsAtom atomFamily Folder items cache by folder ID libraryStatusAtom LibraryStatus Library loading status

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always use folderItemsAtom for folder contents - Don't make direct API calls
  2. Use useRootItems for root items - Provides cache-aware access
  3. Let StorageContext manage loading - Components should read from atoms, not trigger loads
  4. Cache is automatically updated - No manual cache invalidation needed

What you achieve

A library is a folder in your own storage together with everything Common Knowledge Scout knows about it: the documents made from your files, the gallery, the website and the settings. After this guide you have a library that points at your files and is ready for processing.

Language of the interface

Most of the interface is in German. This guide gives the label as it appears on screen, followed by an English translation.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You are signed in.
  • You know where the files are: on the server's file system, in OneDrive or in Nextcloud.
  • For OneDrive you need the tenant ID, client ID and client secret of an app registration. For Nextcloud you need the WebDAV address, your user name and an app password.

docs.title: Step 1: Add a storage connection
docs.text:
Skip this step if the files are on the server's file system.

Access to OneDrive and Nextcloud belongs to your account, not to a single library. You sign in once and use the connection for as many libraries as you like. The credentials are stored encrypted.

  1. Open Settings → Speicher-Verbindungen (storage connections).
  2. Click Neue Verbindung (new connection).
  3. Enter a Bezeichnung (name) and choose the Typ:
    • Nextcloud (WebDAV): WebDAV address, user name, app password.
    • OneDrive (Microsoft 365): tenant ID, client ID, client secret.
  4. Click Anlegen (create).
  5. For OneDrive, click Anmelden (sign in) on the new card and complete the Microsoft sign-in.
  6. Click Testen (test) to confirm that the connection works.

A connection cannot be deleted while a library uses it.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the library
docs.text:
1. On the start page, click Neue Bibliothek (new library). The same entry is in the library switcher at the top of the page.
  2. Go through the steps of the dialog. Three things are required; everything else is a recommendation you can change later.
Step What you decide Required Grundlagen (basics) The name and what the library will contain, for example books and documents, or events and sessions. You can copy the configuration of an existing library of the same kind. Name, content type Quelle (source) Where the files are: Nextcloud, OneDrive or a local directory on the server. For cloud storage you choose a connection and a folder on it; for local storage you enter an absolute path. Yes Verarbeitung (processing) How files are transformed by default No Finden (finding) How visitors explore the gallery No Story How answers to questions are given No Erfassen (capture) Forms for adding new content. Shown only for content types that have them. No Zusammenfassung (summary) A review of your choices –
  1. Click Bibliothek anlegen (create library).

The library appears in the library switcher. Open Archive in the top navigation to see its files.

docs.title: Step 3: Invite people
docs.text:
Only the owner of a library can do this.

  1. Open Settings → Personen (people).
  2. Click Person einladen (invite a person).
  3. Enter the e-mail address, choose a role and, if you like, add a personal message.
Role What the person can do Leser (reader) Read the library Mitwirkender (contributor) Submit content, but not publish it Co-Creator Work in the archive, gallery, story mode and templates, without access to the settings Moderator Handle access requests and send invitations

docs.title: Where the settings are
docs.text:
Section What it controls Library Name and basic settings Archive Storage source, content type and processing defaults Explore How visitors browse the gallery Story How answers sound and which rules they follow Fragen & Antworten (questions and answers) Stored answers Erweitert (advanced) Search and models, storage of twins, extraction, maintenance Personen (people) Members and roles Öffentlicher Auftritt (public presence) Publishing the library Zugriffsanfragen (access requests) Requests from people who want access Mein Zugang, Speicher-Verbindungen Your account: agent access and storage connections

To change the storage of an existing library, open Settings → Archive → Quelle (source).

docs.title: Operate a library with an AI agent
What you achieve
docs.text:
An AI agent such as Claude works on your library for you: it checks what has been processed, starts transformations, publishes pages, changes settings and measures the quality of answers. It does this through an MCP server that is part of Common Knowledge Scout.

Every tool calls the same function as the user interface. There is no second set of rules for agents.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You are signed in and own at least one library.
  • The operator of your instance has enabled the MCP server (see Configuration). If it is not enabled, the server answers with HTTP 503.
  • You use Claude Desktop. This is the client the application ships an extension for.

docs.title: Connect Claude Desktop
docs.text:
The settings page for this is in German.

  1. Open Settings → Mein Zugang and find the card Claude-Zugang (MCP).
  2. Click Erweiterung herunterladen (.mcpb). The downloaded file contains the address of your instance and a personal key.
  3. In Claude Desktop, open Settings → Extensions, choose to install an extension and select the file.
  4. Ask Claude to list your libraries. If it answers with their names, the connection works.

Things to know about the key:

  • It is never displayed. It exists only inside the downloaded file.
  • Each download creates a new key. An extension installed from an older download stops working.
  • It acts as you. The key has the full rights of your account in all your libraries and cannot be limited to reading. Give it only to an agent you would trust with write access.
  • You can withdraw it with Schlüssel widerrufen on the same card.

docs.title: What the agent can do
docs.text:
The server offers 80 tools (tool set 2.70.0). Tool names are German.

Area Examples What they do Libraries and storage bibliotheken_auflisten, bibliothek_anlegen, speicher_verbindung_testen List and create libraries, test and assign storage connections Files ordner_listen, datei_lesen, datei_patchen, verschieben Read, write, move and delete files and folders in the library's storage Coverage and twins abdeckung_scannen, twins_pruefen, twins_synchronisieren Find sources that are not processed yet, check and repair shadow twins Transformation and jobs quelle_erschliessen, transformation_starten, batch_bilanz, batch_neustart Transcribe or extract a source, apply a template, summarise a batch run, restart failed jobs Web capture webseite_erschliessen, playlist_erschliessen Import a web page or a video playlist as sources Documents and index dokumente_auflisten, bestand_pruefen, index_aktualisieren List gallery entries, audit the index, rebuild it from existing transformations Publishing dokument_publizieren, seite_pruefen, veroeffentlichung_setzen Publish and withdraw documents, check the website, change publishing settings Configuration konfiguration_lesen, konfiguration_setzen Read and change the library's chat and gallery configuration, with the same validation as the settings form Questions frage_stellen, golden_set_fahren, fragen_log, antworten_verwerfen Ask story mode a question, run a fixed set of test questions, review and discard stored answers Log protokoll_lesen, bruecke_info Read why actions ran; report the tool set version and what changed

docs.title: Rules the tools follow
docs.text:
• Writing needs a reason. Every tool that changes something requires a short reason and records it in an action log, which protokoll_lesen reads back.
  • Batches are limited. A batch takes up to 30 sources, a folder batch up to 200. An error is reported for the affected row; the rest of the batch continues.
  • Long work runs as a job. A tool call has to finish within about 60 seconds. Anything longer is started as a job, and the agent asks for its status.
  • Working folders are skipped. Batches never enter folders whose name starts with _, or test/.
  • Nothing is assumed silently. When a check cannot run or a value is invalid, the tool says so and does not fall back to a default.

docs.title: Ready-made procedures
docs.text:
The repository contains instructions ("skills") that guide an agent through a complete task:

Skill Task veranstaltung-aufbereiten Take the recordings and slides of an event to published pages, with a stop for a person to review the transcripts webseite-erschliessen Turn a web article or a video playlist into gallery documents website-publishing Create, check and publish the pages of a library's website archiv-aufraeumen Bring a folder in order: check coverage, process what is missing, name files consistently

They are in .claude/skills/ and are written in German.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text:
• Claude sees fewer or different tools than expected. Claude Desktop keeps a copy of the tool list. Switch the extension off and on under Settings → Extensions; bruecke_info shows which tools the server expects.
  • Access is refused (401). The key was replaced by a newer download or withdrawn. Download the extension again and reinstall it.
  • Service unavailable (503). The MCP server is not configured on this instance.

docs.title: Publish a gallery and a website
What you achieve
docs.text:
People can browse the documents of your library without signing in, at an address of its own. If you want more than a gallery, the library also gets a website whose pages you write as Markdown files in your storage.

Language of the interface

Most of the interface is in German. This guide gives the label as it appears on screen, followed by an English translation.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You own the library.
  • At least one file has gone through all three processing steps (see Transform files into documents).

docs.title: Open the library to the public
docs.text:
1. Open Settings → Öffentlicher Auftritt (public presence).
  2. Switch on Library veröffentlichen (publish library).
  3. Enter the Web-Adresse (Slug): lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It must be unique on the instance.
  4. Fill in Öffentlicher Name (public name) and Öffentliche Beschreibung (public description).
  5. Click Veröffentlichung speichern (save).

The library is now available at /explore/<slug>. The form shows the link.

Further options on the same page:

Option Effect Zugriff nur für freigegebene Benutzer (access for approved users only) Visitors must sign in and be approved Auf der Startseite anzeigen (show on the start page) The library appears as a card on the start page of the instance, with the icon and Hintergrundbild (background image) you choose Sterne-Zahl öffentlich zeigen (show star counts publicly) Visitors see how many stars a document has. The names of the people who gave them are never shown. Galerie-Texte (gallery texts) Headline, subtitle, introduction, an explanation of the filters, and the name of the gallery in the menu Bezeichnung eines Eintrags (name of an entry) What a document is called in this library, singular and plural, for example "measure" and "measures"

docs.title: Which documents are visible
docs.text:
A document appears in the gallery once the step Story publizieren has run for it. Each document is either published or a draft. Drafts are hidden from visitors and are not used to answer their questions.

In the gallery, as owner, switch to the table view to see the status of each document and to use Publish, Unpublish and Publish all.

docs.title: What visitors see
docs.text:
The gallery has two views, and every visitor can switch between them:

View For What it shows Simple People who come to read Compact cards, filters in a drawer, a short introduction, and a switch between the documents in focus and all documents Expert People who work with the material All tools: table and graph views, full filters, story mode

In focus is the ranking by stars that members of the library have given. Under Settings → Explore you choose which view opens first and whether the gallery starts in focus or with all entries.

Useful addresses:

Address Opens /explore/<slug> The website if there is one, otherwise the gallery /explore/<slug>?view=gallery The gallery /explore/<slug>?mode=story Story mode /explore/<slug>?site=<page> A page of the website

docs.title: Add a website
docs.text:
A website is a set of Markdown files in the library. Each file is one page.

  1. Create the pages as Markdown files, by convention in the folder Webseite/Seiten/.

  2. Give each page front matter. The front matter is flat: one level of snake_case keys.

    ---
detailViewType: website
title: About
slug: about
menu_order: 2
hero_layout: band
hero_title: About this project
---

  3. Structure the body with sections:

    <!-- section layout=image-left -->
## Why we do this
Text of the section.
<!-- /section -->

  4. Process each page like any other file, so that it is published.

  5. In Settings → Öffentlicher Auftritt, switch on Website am Slug anzeigen (show website at the slug) and set the Website-Logo.
Front matter Purpose title, slug, menu_order, menu_area Name in the menu, address, position, and whether the page is in the main menu, the footer or hidden hero_layout, hero_title, hero_subtitle, hero_image, cta_label, cta_url The opening area of the page and its button banner_tag, banner_title, banner_limit, banner_sort A row of documents from the gallery on the page Section layout Content text-only, image-left, image-right, full-image, video Text and media banner Documents from the gallery story A question box that answers from the library, with example questions. One per page. contact-form A contact form

Inside a section, the blocks <!-- cards -->, <!-- stats -->, <!-- chips --> and <!-- box --> add tiles, figures, tags and highlighted text.

The complete syntax is in the website contract (German). An agent can create, check and publish the pages for you; see Operate a library with an AI agent.

docs.title: Use your own domain
docs.text: The operator of the instance maps a domain to your library with the setting PUBLIC_DOMAIN_LIBRARY_MAP, for example {"example.org":"my-library"}. The domain then shows the library's website at /, without the navigation of the application. See Configuration.

docs.title: Embed the gallery in another website
docs.text:
The package @ks/embed provides the gallery and story mode as a React component:

import '@ks/embed/styles.css'
import { KnowledgeScoutExplorer } from '@ks/embed'

<KnowledgeScoutExplorer
  baseUrl="https://your-instance.example"
  library="my-library"
  view="gallery"
  locale="en"
/>

The embedded component shows only what is visible without signing in. It has no sign-in of its own, and libraries that require one are not shown. The package is built from this repository; it is not published to a public registry.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: • Ask questions in story mode

docs.title: What you achieve
docs.text: You ask a question in your own words and get an answer written from the documents of the library, with a numbered reference to every document it used. You can check each statement against its source.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The library has published documents (see Transform files into documents).
  • For visitors without an account, the library is public (see Publish a gallery and a website).

docs.title: Open story mode
docs.text:
• Choose Story Mode in the navigation of the library, or
  • click View in Story Mode in the gallery or in a document, or
  • open /explore/<slug>?mode=story.

The screen has three parts:

Part Content Chronicle (left) The topics of the library, your earlier questions, and New session Middle A topic overview generated from the library's documents, the questions suggested for each topic, and the conversation Evidence (right) The documents an answer cites

docs.title: Set your perspective
docs.text:
The first time you open story mode, a dialog asks How should answers be formulated for you? You can reopen it at any time with Adjust perspective.

Setting Choices Language The language of the answers Thematic Interests Up to five, for example technology, society and culture, ecology and sustainability, education and learning Access Perspective Up to five, for example insight-oriented, practice-oriented, future-oriented Language Style One of scientific, generally understandable, youth-oriented, professional, child-friendly, simple language and others Advanced Settings The language model

The perspective changes how an answer is worded and what it emphasises. It does not change which documents are available.

docs.title: Ask a question
docs.text:
1. Pick one of the suggested questions of a topic, or open the question box with the round button at the bottom right and type your own.
  2. Choose the Answer length: Short, Medium, Detailed or Unlimited.
  3. Send the question. While the answer is written, the steps are shown in plain words.

Each answer comes with:

  • Citation numbers in the text. One number stands for one document. Click a number to jump to that document in the evidence column.
  • Evidence cards that show how many passages of the document were used and, where known, the page.
  • Other documents found: documents that matched the question but were not cited.
  • Follow-up questions that you can ask with one click.

Next to your question you find Ask again and Delete question.

docs.title: Limit a question with filters
docs.text: Filters you set in the gallery stay active in story mode. A question then searches only the documents that match them. The active filters are shown as chips next to the document counts.

docs.title: How an answer is found
docs.text:
The question is compared by meaning, not by keywords, with the passages of all documents. The passages that fit best are given to the language model together with your question, your perspective and the rules of the library. The model writes the answer from these passages and marks which document each statement comes from.

Answers are stored. When the same question is asked again under the same conditions, the stored answer is shown.

docs.title: For library owners: shape the answers
docs.text:
Where What you set Settings → Story → Antwortregeln (answer rules) Instructions every answer must follow, written as text. They can refer to the values of a metadata field, for example the status of a measure, so that something rejected is not described as decided. Settings → Story → Benannte Regelsätze (named rule sets) Alternative sets of rules. A story section on the website selects one with rules=. Settings → Erweitert → Suche & KI (search and models) The meaning of each value of a metadata field, and the models used Settings → Öffentlicher Auftritt What a document is called, for example "5 talks cited"

After an answer is written, it is checked against the metadata of the cited documents. The result is added as a note below the answer; the text of the answer is not changed.

docs.title: For library owners: review stored answers
docs.text:
Settings → Fragen & Antworten (questions and answers) lists every stored question with its date, language, model, number of sources and state:

State Meaning aktuell (current) The answer matches the present rules and documents veraltet (outdated) The rules, the metadata values or the number of documents have changed since the answer was written verworfen (discarded) You have discarded the answer; the question will be answered afresh next time

Verwerfen discards one answer, Alle Antworten verwerfen all of them. Nothing is deleted; discarded answers stay in the log.

docs.title: Who can ask
docs.text:
• In a public library, anyone can ask without an account.
  • Drafts are used only for owners and moderators. Visitors and signed-in people who are not members get answers from published documents only.

docs.text: • Operate a library with an AI agent – ask questions and measure answers with a fixed set of test questions

docs.title: What you achieve
docs.text:
A recording, a PDF or an image in your storage becomes a structured document with a title, a summary and metadata, and that document becomes searchable. The original file is not changed.

Language of the interface

Most of the interface is in German. This guide gives the label as it appears on screen, followed by an English translation.

docs.title: The three steps of processing
docs.text:
Step Label in the interface What it produces 1. Extract Transkript erstellen (create transcript) The plain text of the source: a transcript for audio and video, recognised text for PDFs, images and office files 2. Transform Artefakte generieren (generate artefacts) A document shaped by a template: front matter with metadata, a structured body and, if you want, a cover image 3. Publish Story publizieren (publish story) The document is split into passages and indexed, so that it appears in the gallery and can be used to answer questions

Each step can be switched on or off, and each can be repeated on its own. The result of steps 1 and 2 is called the shadow twin of the source. It is stored in the database; a library can be set to write a copy as Markdown files into your storage as well.

Supported sources: PDF, audio (mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, opus, flac), video (mp4, mov, avi, webm, mkv, mpeg), images, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, and Markdown. Markdown files skip step 1.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A library with connected storage (see Create a library).
  • The Secretary Service is running. It does the transcription and text recognition.

docs.title: Process one file
docs.text:
1. Open Archive and select the file.
  2. In the preview, open the sheet Aufbereiten & Publizieren (prepare and publish).
  3. Switch on the steps you want. A badge shows whether a result exists already and whether it will be overwritten.
  4. Set the options:
    • Transcript: source and target language for audio and video. For audio you can add context such as the topic and special terms.
    • Artefacts: the Vorlage (template), the language, the model, whether to generate a cover image, and optional notes for corrections.
  5. Click Jetzt starten (start now).

A progress bar in the preview shows the run. When it is finished, the tabs Original, Transkript, Transformation, Story and Uebersicht (overview) show the source and each result. To redo a step, use Neu generieren (regenerate) or Erneut publizieren (publish again) in the corresponding tab.

docs.title: Process a whole folder
docs.text:
1. In Archive, open the folder.
  2. Click Verzeichnis verarbeiten (process directory) in the header. To process only some files, tick them in the list first.
  3. Choose the steps. Erzwingen (force) repeats a step for files that have a result already.
  4. Optionally give the run a name and limit it with a file name pattern; * is the wildcard.
  5. Click Jobs starten (start jobs).

The folder and all its subfolders are scanned. Template, language and extraction method come from the library's defaults. Folders whose name starts with _, and folders named test or tests, are skipped; the dialog shows how many.

docs.title: Follow progress and errors
docs.text: Open the job monitor from the header of the application. It lists the running and finished jobs, can be filtered by run, shows the error of a failed job under Details anzeigen (show details), and restarts failed jobs.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
A template decides what the document looks like. It consists of the metadata fields to fill, instructions for the language model and the layout of the body. Templates are managed under Templates in the top navigation, where you can also test one against a file.

The folder template-samples/ in the repository contains examples that can be imported.

docs.title: Web pages and video playlists
docs.text: Importing a web article together with its embedded audio or video, or a whole video playlist, is available through the agent tools, not through the interface. See Operate a library with an AI agent.
